newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World Dev touted as China play.
newsitem.headline: New World Dev touted as China play.

text.p: A recent flurry to gain exposure to China has sent valuations of red chips skyrocketing and investors have been seeking a cheaper alternative in blue chip New World Development Co Ltd, brokers said on Monday.
New World Development shares have risen 16.03 percent since the end of March compared with a gain of 6.90 percent in the Hang Seng Index and 8.75 percent in the properties sub-index.
The stock rose HK$2.80 on Monday to close at HK$48.50.

"Obviously sentiment towards China stocks has been pretty positive and New World is considered to have a very large and very good China land bank," said Michael Leary, senior property analyst at Lehman Brothers.
In a recent report, Merrill Lynch said New World's (NWD) forward price/earnings multiple remained in the low-teens.
"It may appear as an interesting alternative to "red-chips" which are trading at P/Es of above 20 times," it said.
"While at present the group's China businesses contribute about 10-15 percent of its bottom line, the share is poised to increase in the years ahead as more projects come to fruition."
Red chips are Hong Kong-incorporated companies with financial backing from China.

ING Barings said New World had found itself a profitable niche in the China property market with the development of government subsidised housing and was "in a strong position to become the largest property developer in China".
In a recent report it said New World had about 10 million square metres (105 million sq ft) of gross floor area in seven government subsidised housing projects encompassing five cities.
"We believe NWD is several years ahead of the competition in terms of development progress and the size and location of its landbank," it said.

"The New World group is beginning to benefit from the investments it has made in China since 1989, with the most significant earnings contribution coming from infrastructure projects," ING Barings said.

It said China projects at subsidiary New World Infrastructure Ltd accounted for 4.2 percent of New World Development's net profits in fiscal 1996 and this was expected to rise to 7.6 percent by fiscal 1999.

ING Barings said government subsidised housing, the group's second investment in China, should contribute HK$91 million to earnings in fiscal 1997, up 350 percent from the previous year, to account for 1.7 percent of full-year fiscal 1997 forecasts.
ING Barings, which has a buy recommendation on the stock, forecast net profit for the year to June 30 of HK$5.27 billion compared with HK$4.16 billion in 1995/96.
It forecast 1997/1998 net profit of HK$7.09 billion.

"Stripping out exceptional items, we forecast NWD to post about 40 percent earnings growth per annum in FY97 and FY98, and eight percent for FY99," said Merrill Lynch, which also rates the stock a buy.

It said New World may produce exceptional items in coming years "as we envisage continued restructuring within NWD, such as the potential spin-off (of) its construction operations and its investments in China properties and industrial projects".
